blocks.content: Article 32 is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.

rows: Enforcement of Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights
Applicable across the entire territory of India
Limited to state boundaries or specific High Court jurisdiction

items: The term 'Budget' does not exist in the Indian Constitution; Article 112 officially uses the term 'Annual Financial Statement'.
Articles 20 and 21 remain enforceable even during an Emergency declared under Article 352.
Article 226 gives High Courts broader writ jurisdiction than Article 32 gives to the Supreme Court, as Article 226 covers legal rights in addition to Fundamental Rights.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 32 grants the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and was called the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
Article 21 (Right to Life) and Article 20 (Protection in respect of conviction for offenses) cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.
Article 112 refers to the 'Annual Financial Statement', as the word 'Budget' is nowhere mentioned in the Indian Constitution.
Article 368 empowers Parliament to amend the Constitution and its procedure.
Article 44 deals with the Uniform Civil Code, listed under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
